title: MDQ Specification Audit: multiple-choice
scope: The `multiple-choice` question type: `docs/question-types/multiple-choice.md`, `schema/multiple-choice.yaml`, its grammar, and the shared specs it depends on (`docs/references/grammar.md`, `docs/references/patterns.md`, `docs/question-types/question-base.md`, `docs/exam.md`, `docs/responses.md`).
methodology:
Automated checks: `uv run scripts/spec_audit.py` passed all 14 steps before the audit (schema bundle, docs, Additional Rules, lint codes, valid and invalid corpus, frontmatter tables, property consistency, code blocks, schema agreement).

Manual review: the lead auditor read the shared specs and the multiple-choice spec and recorded contradictions, ambiguities, omissions and inconsistencies. A grammar subagent turned the multiple-choice grammar and the shared grammar into Lark grammars and tested what they accept and reject against the stated rules. A second, independent subagent reviewed the multiple-choice spec against `schema/multiple-choice.yaml`, ran every complete example through `mdq validate`, and checked the Additional Rules table against the MUST/SHOULD/MAY statements of the text.

strengths.text: The `score` range, the `choices` minimum, the `id` SLUG pattern, and the `grading`/`shuffle` enums and `inherit` defaults agree between multiple-choice.md and schema/multiple-choice.yaml.
The `grading` and `shuffle` inheritance rules agree between multiple-choice.md, exam.md and the schema descriptions (`inherit` default, `symmetric`/`false` outside an exam).
The six rows of the grading table match the formula u = clamp(-Σspecified / #unspecified, -1, 0), including both clamp cases.

The `value` and `percent` rules of the multiple-choice item match the prose and the examples. Tested with Lark: accepted `[*]`, `[ ]`, `[\t]`, `[  ]`, `[ * ]`, `[ 50% ]`, `[100%]`, `[+50%]`, `[33.5%]`, `[-100%]`, `[150%]` (left to the schema range check, as the prose says); rejected `[]` (parse-error, as in examples/invalid/multiple-choice-empty-brackets), `[x]`, `[**]`, `[.5%]`, `[5.%]`, `[U+00A0]` and `[U+000B]`. Each of these accepted values has exactly one semantic parse.

The shared rules `ws`, `nl` and `SLUG` hold. `ws` accepts space, tab and mixes, and rejects U+00A0, U+3000, U+000B, U+000C and U+FEFF. `nl` accepts LF, CR and CRLF (CRLF as one line ending), and rejects U+000B, U+000C, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. `SLUG` accepts `Q1`, `ipe-amarelo`, `a_b`, `a-b_c` and `1`, and rejects `a--b`, `-a`, `a-`, `a_`, `ipê`, `a b`, `a.b` and the empty string, in Python `re` (Lark) and JavaScript `RegExp`. A U+00A0 before the item and in the value is rejected, and a U+2028 inside choice text stays text, as the prose of grammar.md requires.

`UNICODE_SPACE` matches exactly the 25 code points of the Unicode White_Space property (Python `str.isspace()` minus U+001C to U+001F) in Python `re`, and 25 code points in JavaScript `RegExp` with and without the `u` flag. `UNIT` excludes exactly `UNICODE_SPACE` plus `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`. The regex-dialect claims hold: JavaScript `\s` matches U+FEFF and not U+0085 or U+001C; Python `\s` matches U+0085 and U+001C and not U+FEFF.

Every row of the multiple-choice symmetric grading table matches the formula -(sum of declared scores)/(unspecified count) clamped to [-1, 0], and examples/grading/multiple-choice.yaml repeats each row as a test case.

The multiple-choice schema agrees with the prose on score range [-1, 1] (malformed, not clamped), the choice id pattern (the SLUG terminal of grammar.md), minItems 2, and the grading/shuffle enums and `inherit` defaults of exam.md Inheritance.
The three complete multiple-choice documents in the spec (capital of Brazil, exclamation mark, largest river) validate with mdq-py without errors or warnings.

The corpus covers most multiple-choice edge cases: percent forms (+50%, 33.5%, 0%, -100%), spaced and tab values, both feedback/comment orders, continuation lines, link at choice start, out-of-range score, empty brackets, foreign marker, single choice, duplicate id/text, all-correct and no-correct cases.

risks: The multiple-choice item is specified three times (grammar, prose, Additional Rules) and the three disagree on empty text, empty feedback, interleaving, continuation lines and choice ids; mdq-py follows a fourth reading in some cases, so mdq-js has no single source to port.
The choice item has no Markdown-to-AST mapping, so the JSON/YAML form of a question is defined only by the corpus and by mdq-py.

Lint severities and verbs (MAY reject, MAY warn, critical vs warning for blanks) do not match between the type spec, question-base and lint-codes.md, so the reported level depends on which document an implementer reads.
